market.question: Will the 30-year Treasury yield dip below 5.12% in September?

en.title: 30Y Yield Dip Unlikely
en.summary: The probability of the 30-year Treasury yield dipping below 5.12% in September plummeted by 34.5% to 6%. This sharp decline was driven by recent strong jobs data and sustained high bond yields, as highlighted by headlines linking them to market pressure.
drivers: Stronger-than-expected jobs data.
Sustained high bond yields.
Expectations of prolonged higher Fed rates.
en.why_matters: Higher long-term Treasury yields impact borrowing costs for governments and corporations, potentially slowing economic growth and affecting asset valuations across markets.
en.bull_case: A significant economic downturn or a dovish shift from the Federal Reserve could quickly push yields below 5.12%.
en.bear_case: Continued robust economic growth and persistent inflation fears will keep the 30-year Treasury yield well above 5.12%.
